solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Perhaps Robinson Crusoe players off on tour (8)

blocks.note: the cast = the players in a production
a touring side is away from home

explanation.surface: A theatre company takes its Robinson Crusoe production on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a touring play, so 'players' reads as actors in a show, which is exactly the CAST. 'Perhaps' warns that Crusoe is just one example of a castaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinson Crusoe was shipwrecked and marooned on an island, the classic castaway.

clue.text: In centres of reactors, high explosive holds together (7)

indicators.note: 'In' places one thing inside another, so HE sits in the centres, the CORES

blocks.note: a reactor's core is its centre
HE is the standard abbreviation for high explosive

explanation.surface: A nuclear-safety worry about explosives at the heart of reactors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centres of' looks like an instruction to take middle letters of 'reactors', but it is a plain synonym: reactor centres are CORES.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to stick together as a whole, so it holds together.

clue.text: Get out first piece of stored stuff (5)

indicators.note: the first piece of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: opening letter of 'stored'
to stuff = to cram

explanation.surface: Someone clearing out a storage unit, getting the first item out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' reads as a noun, things in storage, but it is the verb to stuff, CRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is a brusque order to go away, the same as 'Get out!'.

clue.text: Crazy idea, normal for teenage diarist (6,4)

indicators.note: the letters of IDEA NORMAL go crazy into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: An odd pairing: a crazy idea passing as normal for a teenager keeping a diary.
explanation.walkthrough: Adrian Mole is the hero of Sue Townsend's comic novels, written as the diary of an anxious English teenager.
explanation.definitionFit: The Secret Diary of Adrian Mole, Aged 13¾ makes him the best-known fictional teenage diarist in Britain.

clue.text: A sweetheart embraces Charlie in quiet corner (6)

indicators.note: LOVE wraps its arms around C

blocks.note: taken as written
a sweetheart is one's love
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A couple cuddling in a secluded nook: the sweetheart embraces Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie looks like the sweetheart's partner, but he is only a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove is a recess set back in a wall, a quiet corner of a room.

clue.text: Beautiful female with distinctive appearance (4)

blocks.note: F is the standard abbreviation for female
an air is a distinctive manner or look, as in 'an air of mystery'

explanation.surface: Describing a striking woman: beautiful, with a look all her own.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as one description of a woman, but 'Beautiful' alone is the definition and the rest builds F plus AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in its old sense means beautiful, as in 'fair maiden'.

clue.text: Advise of a very quiet pay increase (7)

blocks.note: taken as written
pp = pianissimo, the musical mark for very quiet
a pay rise, the British term for a raise

explanation.surface: An employee being told, very discreetly, about a raise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very quiet' seems to describe how the raise is handled; it is the music marking PP.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprise someone is to inform or advise them of something.

clue.text: Was responsible for church estate (5)

blocks.note: to run something is to be in charge of it
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone who once managed a church's land.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface joins 'responsible for' as one phrase; 'for' actually belongs between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farming estate, especially for cattle.

clue.text: Grand car here, ordered for the duchess (3,5)

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: G = grand, a thousand
anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: A servant told to bring the grand car round for the duchess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as a command to a chauffeur, but it rearranges the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Her Grace is the formal style used when speaking of a duchess, so the title stands in for the woman herself.

clue.text: Quickly turn page in grave error (4)

indicators.note: 'In' reads literally: the page is placed in the error, P inside SIN

blocks.note: a sin is a grave moral error
P is the standard abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: Hastily turning a page to hide a serious mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn page' looks like one action, but 'Quickly turn' is the definition and the page is only P.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a top or a dancer that spins whirls round fast, and the clue's two words cover both speed and motion.

clue.text: Sportswoman excited at her title (10)

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A champion thrilled at winning her title.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is the champion's own reaction: excited at her title.
explanation.definitionFit: A triathlete competes in swimming, cycling and running; 'Sportswoman' is a fair example, not a definition by gender.

clue.text: Strum balalaika, holding a dance (5)

indicators.note: the words hold the answer inside them

blocks.note: stRUM BAlalaika

explanation.surface: A musician strumming a balalaika while a dance goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: The music setting makes a dance natural, which helps hide RUMBA across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the rumba, born in Cuba and later taken into the ballroom, is one dance among many.

clue.text: Tons of tarnish replaced with very glossy coat (7)

indicators.note: one letter swaps in for another

blocks.note: the word to be changed
T = tons; this T comes out
V = very; it goes in where T was

explanation.surface: Advice on covering up tarnish with a shiny finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Tarnish and varnish are both about surfaces, so the swap of T for V hides in a plausible DIY tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Varnish is a clear liquid that dries to a hard glossy coat.

clue.text: Text message about father’s cramps (6)

indicators.note: 'About' in its sense of 'around', so the message wraps round father's

blocks.note: SMS is the technical name for a text message
PA'S = father's

explanation.surface: A text arriving to say that Dad has cramp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as 'concerning', a message about Dad, but here it is positional. SMS stands for Short Message Service, the system behind phone texts.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasms are sudden involuntary muscle contractions, which is what cramps are.

clue.text: Holster, could one say, that may be beside you as you sit down? (7)

definitions.text: that may be beside you as you sit down

blocks.note: 'arm' can mean a weapon, and a holster is where a gun sits idle; 'could one say' flags the pun

blocks.clueFragment: that may be beside you as you sit down
blocks.note: the padded side of a chair

explanation.surface: A riddle about something at your side when you take a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a pun: a holster is where an arm, meaning a gun, rests, so it is an 'arm rest'; 'could one say' flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: An armrest is the part of a chair beside you where your arm rests as you sit.

clue.text: Worries before small stroke (6)

indicators.note: 'Before' means placed in front of, so the worries come first and the small letter follows

blocks.note: cares = worries
S is the standard abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Someone fretting before suffering a minor stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'stroke' medical; it is the gentle touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the gentle sense of 'stroke', a soft touch of the hand, not the medical one.

clue.text: Fine line intercepted by transmitter (7)

blocks.note: a sender transmits
L is the standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A phone line being tapped by a radio transmitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine line' reads as one phrase, but 'Fine' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, using 'fine' in its sense of thin or delicate, as with fine hair, not excellent or a penalty.

clue.text: Composer finally changes into a god (6)

indicators.note: the last letter is changed into another

blocks.note: Johannes Brahms, the German composer; his final S goes
the A that replaces the S

explanation.surface: A composer transformed into a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAHMS becomes BRAHMA by one letter; 'finally' points at the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Brahma, the creator in Hindu belief, is one of many gods.

clue.text: One taking a trip may have a generous whisky here (7)

definitions.text: may have a generous whisky here

blocks.note: a trip here is a stumble, so this is someone who falls over

blocks.clueFragment: may have a generous whisky here
blocks.note: a wide flat-bottomed glass, the kind a large whisky is poured into

explanation.surface: A traveller enjoying a large whisky on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking a trip' reads as travelling, but it means tripping over: a tumbler is one who falls.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbler is one who tumbles, and also a flat-bottomed glass that holds a generous whisky.

clue.text: Subject to snap (5)

blocks.note: taken as written
a snap is a photo, a pic

explanation.surface: Something liable to break suddenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject to snap' reads as 'liable to break'; 'Subject' is a noun and 'snap' a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with 'Subject' as the noun, the matter under discussion, not the adjective the surface suggests.

clue.text: Takes hot drink, unfinished in hurry (5)

blocks.note: to have a drink is to take it
TEA without its final A

explanation.surface: Someone gulping a hot drink and leaving it half-drunk in a rush.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a coffee left behind in a rush; the rush itself is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is hurry, as in 'more haste, less speed'.

clue.text: Relax around place for break (5)

indicators.note: 'Around' means surrounding, so relax wraps round place

blocks.note: to sit back = to relax
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Advice to unwind somewhere during a work break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' looks like a rest from work, which suits 'Relax'; it is the verb to break, SPLIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: wood or a vase that splits has broken.

clue.text: Skin: what it does after too much sun? (4)

definitions.text: what it does after too much sun

blocks.note: the rind of a fruit

blocks.clueFragment: what it does after too much sun
blocks.note: sunburnt skin comes away in flakes

explanation.surface: A wry note on sunburnt skin.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a phrase standing for a verb: sunburnt skin peels.
explanation.definitionFit: Peel is the skin of a fruit, and sunburnt skin peels off.

clue.text: Coaxed with caution, came to the front (8)

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for with
to take heed is to take care
to lead is to be at the front

explanation.surface: Someone cautiously coaxed out into the open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like part of the phrase 'with caution', but it is the letter W.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheedle is to coax someone with flattery.

clue.text: Appealing to reduce energy (4)

blocks.note: to cut = to reduce
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A plea for lower energy use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appealing' reads as 'pleading', but it means attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute means attractive in an endearing way, appealing.

clue.text: Mother more dapper becoming seductress (3-5)

blocks.note: ma = mother
dapper = neat, so more dapper = neater

explanation.surface: Mum smartening herself up and turning into a femme fatale.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a transformation; 'becoming' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eater is a woman who seduces and discards men.
